note: SAME DEPOSIT AND SAME METHOD AS batch_202's gilbert_meta_73, so the reasoning there applies here too. Live codes are the dictionary's variable names with the wave prefix stripped, and the live `wave` column (0 baseline, 0.5 midline, 1 endline) carries what the prefix encoded. The renaming happened upstream of this repo -- data/gilbert_hte/postprocessing.R points at an external 'gilbert_share/06 IL-HTE Econ/analysis/' -- so the correspondence was verified against the data rather than read off a script. ITEM TEXT IS THE TASK DESCRIPTION, NOT A LITERAL ITEM, and that is deliberate rather than a gap: the deposit ships FOUR parallel forms whose content differs, and the live table records no form, so no literal item is a property of an item code. The visible consequence is that item_text repeats across a task family. resp is 0/1 and the deposit publishes no value labels for these variables, so option_text is blank; that 1 means correct follows from makedata.do recoding 9 to 0 and summing the items into test scores, and is recorded in the public note as an inference rather than a transcription. VERIFICATION: 12 of the 33 codes are wave-restricted by the dictionary and all 12 hold in the data -- the nine baseline-only codes (comp1-comp4 comprehension, and the six let_fill boxes) appear at wave 0 alone, and the three endline-only word_dic codes appear at 0.5 and 1 only. The remaining 21 span all three waves as the dictionary implies. That the baseline and endline forms differ in content is itself the finding: the baseline form carried comprehension and letter-filling tasks that the endline forms dropped, and the endline forms added word dictation. A NOTE ON WHAT THESE ITEMS ARE: several are picture-dependent -- matpic ('Encircle the word which matches with the picture'), obj_name ('Look at the picture and write the name of the object') and writpic ('Look at the picture, and write the word') -- so even with a single form there would be no transcribable stem beyond the task, only an image. The task description is the whole of the available text for those nine items regardless of the parallel-forms problem.
public_note: Thirty-three items from the written Hindi language test for standards 1-2, pooled across baseline (wave 0), midline (0.5) and endline (1). IMPORTANT: item_text is the TASK the item asks, not the specific letter, word or passage. The study used four parallel forms with different content and the table does not record which form a child took, so several items share the same item_text. Nine of the items are picture-dependent (matching a word to a picture, naming an object, writing a word from a picture), so for those the task is all the text there is. The form changed across waves: comprehension and letter-filling items appear only at baseline, and word dictation only at the two endlines. resp is 0/1 and the deposit publishes no labels for it; 1 is correct on the evidence of the deposit's own scoring code, which is an inference, so option_text is blank.

VERIFICATION AND A SOURCE ERROR IT FOUND. The wave test is weak on this table -- 19 of its 20 codes are defined in all three waves, so only one code is discriminating -- and that one code exposed a TYPO IN THE DICTIONARY rather than a problem with the mapping. mathwrit_std12_add2d_b is listed with b_ and e2_ prefixes but no e1_, which would mean it was not administered at midline; the data has it at midline. The cause is visible in the sheet: 'Math Aser & Written test-End1' row 8b gives the variable name as e1_mathwrit_std12_add2d_a, duplicating row 8a, while that row's own question label correctly reads 'q8_b Addition-two digit'. So the End1 sheet names add2d_a twice and add2d_b never. The data is right and the dictionary has a one-cell error. It cannot affect what ships: rows 8a and 8b carry the identical task description, 'Addition-two digit'.
